stem: An 8-year-old boy with known severe acute malnutrition presents with about three weeks of cough and worsening lethargy. He has never been treated for TB before. Sputum obtained with coaching, supplemented by a gastric aspirate, was positive for M. tuberculosis; testing confirmed resistance to rifampicin, isoniazid, and fluoroquinolones (pre-XDR-TB), with no other risk factors for resistance beyond this result -- no HIV, no prior treatment. Separately, his older sister was never evaluated for preventive therapy two years ago when an aunt who lived with the family for several months at that time was treated for fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR-TB; the aunt has since completed treatment and is no longer infectious. Exam (patient): severely wasted (known baseline), mild crackles, no lymphadenopathy.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents and older sister; an aunt who previously stayed with the family was treated for MDR-TB two years ago
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough and worsening lethargy, confirmed pre-XDR-TB
patient.exam_findings: Severely wasted (known baseline), mild crackles, no lymphadenopathy
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: The patient's presentation assumed low-risk for resistant TB given the absence of prior treatment, arguing against confirmatory resistance testing

The sister's exposure treated as moot because the aunt has already completed treatment and is cured, rather than considering that preventive therapy was never offered during the actual exposure window
ntep_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.

Offer his sister a fixed, standardized preventive regimen of 6 months of daily levofloxacin as a routine part of programmatic TB preventive treatment for a household contact of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR/RR-TB, once active TB disease is excluded in her, regardless of how long ago the exposure occurred.
who_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.

Offer his sister a fixed, standardized preventive regimen of 6 months of daily levofloxacin as a routine part of programmatic TB preventive treatment for a household contact of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR/RR-TB, once active TB disease is excluded in her, regardless of how long ago the exposure occurred.
us_correct_actions: Reserve rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for patients who meet at least one specific risk criterion (prior TB treatment, birth in or residence in a higher-TB-incidence country, contact with a known MDR-TB case, or HIV infection); do not order it routinely for a patient with none of these risk factors.

Treat offering preventive treatment to his sister as only conditionally appropriate versus observation alone; if treatment is given, individualize the regimen and duration to the source case's (the aunt's) susceptibility pattern rather than using a fixed levofloxacin regimen.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance/confirmatory testing given this child's TB diagnosis
Concluding that no preventive action is warranted for the sister because the aunt has already completed treatment and is cured
expected_divergence_points: Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is performed universally or only for patients meeting specific US risk criteria
Whether household contacts of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR/RR-TB receive a fixed, standardized preventive regimen or an individualized regimen contingent on a conditional decision to treat
